section_1.title: Introduction: The Game as a Decision Tree
section_1.content: Define Wordle as a search problem within a finite set (approx. 2,300 solutions). Introduce the concept of 'information gain'—how a guess reduces the remaining possibilities.
section_1.example: Visualizing a branching tree: Start with 2,300 nodes, each guess acts as a filter that prunes the tree branches.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Entropy
section_2.content: Explain Shannon Entropy. In Wordle, high entropy means a word splits the remaining vocabulary into the most equal-sized groups, providing the most information on average.
section_2.example: Graphical chart: Comparing 'ARISE' (high entropy, splits set into 100-200 groups) vs 'XYLYL' (low entropy, only checks rare letters).

section_3.title: Algorithmic Analysis: Greedy vs. Global Optimal
section_3.content: Discuss the 'Greedy' approach (choosing the best word for the current turn) versus looking ahead. Explain why the highest entropy word isn't always the winner, but provides the best path.
section_3.example: A robot character 'Bot-Bot' testing the word 'CRANE'. Shows a heat map of letter frequency (E, A, R) vs. position frequency.

section_4.title: Putting it Together: Strategy Implementation
section_4.content: Synthesize the strategy: Use high-frequency letter distributions (E, A, R, I, O, T, N, S) in the first move to maximize entropy, then shift to candidate elimination.
section_4.example: Step-by-step animation: Guess 1 (CRANE) -> Feedback (C-gray, R-green, A-yellow...) -> Filter list -> Pick Guess 2 based on highest remaining entropy.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Practical Takeaways
section_5.content: Summarize the 'Optimal Wordle' heuristic: 1. Maximize unique letter coverage; 2. Prioritize common vowels/consonants; 3. Use the feedback to mathematically isolate the solution.
section_5.example: A quick recap screen: An 'Optimal Strategy Cheat Sheet' featuring an owl icon (the symbol of wisdom) showing the top 3 starting words.

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Practical Takeaways", [

        self.place_at_grid(cheat_sheet, 'B2')

            Text("2. SLATE", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text("3. TRACE", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_at_grid(words, 'D3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(cheat_sheet))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Write(words))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Represent closing graphic/owl symbol
        owl = Tex(r"🦉", font_size=72)
        self.place_at_grid(owl, 'E5')
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(owl))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Game as a Decision Tree", [
